body:
adding these lines will make a bunch of test fail related specifically to this behaviour before start. The tests in index seem to make sense to need .started, but the ones in RoutingManager seem like legit bug fixes

I've considered doing something like `_isSsrServer` (passing Vue's `this.$isServer` to instance), but not sure if that makes full sense.
I'm not too sure how to test this, since localUiState isn't exposed outside
I would have put this condition where we mutate the `localUiState` that way it's simpler to reason about.
Could this be passed in the `getLocalWidgetsState` 3rd argument call below? That would be one less mutation and code branch to think about.

If I understand https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4359#issuecomment-623964835 well, you want to pass `localUiState` only at first render, and `{}` next times. Is that right? If not, can you explain when we need to use the current UI state and when we don't want to use it?
or else thought of putting it in here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/9ff71e2341acc5b09133e095c3285a2de162b846/src/widgets/index/index.ts#L362-L366

If I understand correctly, this doesn't have to be `privateHelperSetState` since we're not providing `_isFromAddWidget` here.

What about just reverting it back to `widgetHelper._change({ ... })`?
If we do that, then we use `privateHelperSetState` only in one place and we could rename it to something like `setStateFromAddWidget` to be more explicit.

What do you think?
yes, but that would require us to use _change still, which is a private, so I'd rather use that only in a single function, if that makes sense :)
I didn't know _change was used only here. Then it makes sense to me.
Why is this equality check needed? It didn't seem to be here before the changes.
I'm not sure to understand this change?

(1) Instead of saying where it's from, what about saying what it does? (similarly to `isPageReset`). This name looses sense suddenly if we were to reuse it somewhere else. A suggestion: `_shouldInheritUiState`.

(2) To make it more testable and easier to think about, I would rather pass the `baseUiState` object here, instead of a boolean.
this is code in the helper: https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/blob/develop/src/algoliasearch.helper.js#L1315
I've added a test that highlights how global ui state before this change gets "lost". Without this change nested indices don't receive a UiState to start from
Good suggestion, I've changed it to `_uiState`, where we pass the local ui state in this case
Got it! Can you add [this link](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/blob/6b835ffd07742f2d6b314022cce6848f5cfecd4a/src/algoliasearch.helper.js#L1311-L1324) to the above comment then?

I got confused because of the comment—I think it's fair to remove it.

Although the name is `uiState`, it has always only acted as an initial UI state from the beginning since it's used to initialize the index UI state.

Those seemed to be your thoughts when you were writing code but they're confusing from the outside 😅

Wdyt about removing this?
